text:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION_ALERT triggered for eu-west-1 (severity: P1 -> auto-escalate if not ack in 5m). Queue growth > 4000 requests, throttling rising, autoscaler errors reported. https://internal.monitor/alerts/6754321000

oncall-taylor: Acked. I'm on it. grabbing metrics now.

sre-alex: seeing steady queue increase since 23:12 UTC, 95th latency spiking to 6.2s on text-gen endpoints. Throttles (429) up for batch-generation path.

ml-infra-sam: autoscaler logs show repeated failures to create new gpu pods: "scaleup rejected: hard_pool_limit_exceeded" and occasional provider 503 during node provisioning. Paste from autoscaler: 
```
ERROR 23:18:51 autoscaler.go:421 scaleUp: request failed: quotaExceeded: cannot allocate more G4 pools (limit 12)
WARN 23:19:02 autoscaler.go:429 backoff for pool-create 30s
```

eng-ops: provider quotas look tight in eu-west. We had a burst earlier today from tenant:searchcorp-runner that probably consumed reserved pools.

oncall-taylor: immediate mitigation options?

sre-alex: short term: 1) route lower-priority tenants to cpu-warm pool (fallback model), 2) enable tenant-level rate-limit for heavy tenants, 3) reduce default batch sizes for gen endpoints to avoid enqueue hysteresis.

ml-infra-sam: I can push a routing change to migrate 15% of traffic to cpu-warm models (costly but keeps latency). Doing a canary redirect for non-SLA customers now.

eng-ops: provider support is responding to quota request but ETA 2+ hours. we can't rely on immediate new GPUs.

pm-jess: whats customer impact? any paying customers hitting errors? need comms draft.

support-maria: Support: several customers reported 429s and slow embeddings. Affected: searchcorp, docsly (self-hosted prod), and two sandbox orgs. Searchcorp has high p95 latency and partial failures.

oncall-taylor: ok let's implement mitigations in this order: 1) tenant rate-limits for top-2 heavy tenants, 2) route non-SLA production -> cpu-warm fallback, 3) temporarily lower default batch size for gen endpoint. Sam, Alex, can you split work?

ml-infra-sam: on it — initiating routing change (will proxy 20% non-SLA traffic to cpu-warm fallback). Pushing config now: 
```
PATCH /routing/policies/active
{ "policy": "fallback-cpu-warm", "percent": 20, "target": "cpu-warm-models/v1" }
```

sre-alex: I'll push tenant rate-limits and batch-size override via infra feature flags. Applying "rate_limit: tenant=searchcorp limit=50rps" now.

(2m later)

ml-infra-sam: routing patch applied. initial telemetry: queue length plateaued and ingest rate to gpu pool decreased ~18%. p95 latency trending down.

sre-alex: rate-limits in place for searchcorp & docsly. seeing immediate reduction in 429 spikes. p95 down from 6.2s -> 3.4s on gen path.

eng-ops: manual cluster scale workaround: creating ephemeral cpu fallback increases cost but prevents hard failures. confirming billing approval.

pm-jess: drafting status page: "Degraded performance for generation and embeddings in eu-west-1; we have partial mitigations in place and are routing non-SLA traffic to fallback models." Will post after you confirm impact numbers.

support-maria: please include list of affected customers in internal comms: searchcorp (high), docsly (medium), sandbox-accounts (low). I'm pinging account teams.

incident-bot: NOTE: Automatic paging escalation suppressed (oncall ack).

ml-infra-sam: autoscaler still showing backoff loops but fewer requests now. Provider quota request is being processed but not guaranteed.

eng-ops: observed another problem: GKE node auth intermittently failing on pool-create from autoscaler (500). We've opened ticket with provider; they confirm degraded control-plane in eu-west-1 for GPU SKU.

oncall-taylor: given provider ETA > 2h, next steps: keep fallback routing, monitor queue until < 1000, then gradually lift rate-limits. If queue doesn't stabilize, we run emergency tenant-eviction for non-critical tenants.

pm-jess: status page posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/6754321000 (internal) — will publicize if SLA customers affected > 30 min.

support-maria: Searchcorp CS rep wants a short note to customers: "We're experiencing degraded performance in EU; we have applied temporary routing to reduce errors; engineering investigating. We'll update in 30 minutes."

(20m later)

ml-infra-sam: queue now ~920, GPU pool utilizations down to 78%. p95 gen latency ~2.1s. autoscaler still in backoff but no new create attempts for 8m.

sre-alex: good stabilization. leaving rate-limits and fallback in place for 30 more minutes, then we can step down to 10% fallback.

eng-ops: provider escalated quota request; tentative capacity increase scheduled in 1.5h if provider control-plane healthy.

oncall-taylor: switching to standby oncall (taylor -> taylor) — keep watch. If errors spike again, escalate pager.

pm-jess: action items to capture for postmortem: 
- root cause: provider GPU quota + intermittent control-plane failures prevented autoscaler from provisioning (ml-infra to verify logs)
- immediate mitigations used: routing fallback, tenant rate-limits, batch-size reduction (sre/infra)
- customer impact: searchcorp & docsly experienced 429s and elevated latency for ~45m (support to collect customer logs)
- long-term: add provider health checks into autoscaler decision, add a safer degradation mode (automatic fallback to cpu-warm for X%) and trial emergency tenant-priority scheduler

support-maria: I'll collect SLAs and affected request IDs for searchcorp and docsly and share in #support-postmortems.

ml-infra-sam: I'll add autoscaler unit/regression test that simulates provider quota errors and ensure fallback policy triggers automatically.

sre-alex: I'll update runbook to include quick commands: 
```
# force-route non-SLA to cpu-warm
curl -X PATCH https://internal.api/routing -d '{"policy":"fallback-cpu-warm","percent":20}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# tenant rate-limit
curl -X POST https://internal.api/tenant-limits -d '{"tenant":"searchcorp","rps":50}'
```

eng-ops: I'll follow up on provider quota requests and keep billing/reg approvals for temporary extra capacity.

oncall-taylor: final status: mitigated, not resolved. Monitoring. Will create incident ticket for postmortem and schedule 1h retrospective tomorrow 09:30 UTC. Assign owners: Sam (autoscaler tests + provider fallback) due 2026-03-22, Alex (runbook + batch defaults) due 2026-03-20, Eng-ops (quota follow up) due 2026-03-18, Support (customer impact report) due 2026-03-18.

pm-jess: noted. I'll prepare comms for customers for the postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 30m or on any regression.

sre-alex: logging full incident thread into ops/incident-6754321000 and creating postmortem draft.

support-maria: thanks team — will escalate to account execs for searchcorp.

oncall-taylor: closing handoff, leaving channel open for follow-ups.
